chunks: "A stick of lote-tree." I said: "If we are not able to obtain lote-tree?" He said: "Then a stick of khilāf."
And with this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Bilāl:

He wrote to him asking him about the palm-stalk: if we do not find it, may we place something else in its stead in a place where palm is not available? So he wrote: "It is permissible when the palm-stalk is unavailable, and the palm-stalk is superior." And with this the narration has come.

key_terms.أُعْوِزَتِ: it became unavailable or could not be found
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةُ: the palm-stalk customarily placed with the deceased
key_terms.عُودُ الخِلَافِ: a stick from the khilāf tree mentioned as an alternative substitute
key_terms.عُودُ السِّدْرِ: a stick from the lote-tree used here as a substitute material
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: it is permissible in legal usage

ai.seo_question: What should be used in place of the funerary palm-stalk if it is unavailable?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the use of funerary palm-stalks and their substitutes when the original material is unavailable. It indicates that alternatives may be used out of necessity, while affirming that the prescribed palm-stalk remains preferable.
